title: RequirementSet
description: The container a performance requirement is written into. Deliberately minimal: it fixes the shape and nothing else. Metric and attribute names are plain strings, borrowed from OpenTelemetry rather than defined here, so measuring something new never means changing the format.

indicator.description: What is measured, in one of two shapes, exactly one of them. Modelled on OpenSLO's thresholdMetric/ratioMetric — see ADR-0001 D8 for why the names differ. Nested keys rather than a discriminator, so a decoder needs no second pass.

distribution.description: A distribution of measured values — latency, size. Reduced by a percentile, min, max, avg, stddev or sum.

ratio.description: A fraction of requests: the numerator over the denominator. It names no metric, because nothing here is measured — only counted. `total` is the denominator; `good` or `bad` is the numerator, applied on top of `total` and carrying only what puts a request on that side. This is ADR-0001 D8's shape, and an error rate is a `ratio` with `bad: {error.type: "*"}` — no invented errors metric, which OpenTelemetry does not have either.

bad.description: The numerator: what went wrong. Narrows `total`.

good.description: The numerator: what went right. Exactly one of `bad` or `good`.

name.description: Optional. Identifies this predicate in a report; without it the aggregation is the identifier, so two predicates in one requirement may not then share an aggregation.

guards.description: Preconditions: statements that the run happened in the intended regime at all. Same shape as a criterion, and the difference is what a violation means — a criterion says the system did not hold, a guard says the run did not happen as intended, so a green criterion beside a violated guard is not evidence of anything. Optional, and a requirement without one asserts nothing about the conditions it assumes.

allOf.description: docs/GLOSSARY.md permits only rate and count over a ratio. A percentile of a fraction has no meaning, and nothing downstream could evaluate it.

examples.name: checkout-latency-under-load
examples.displayName: Checkout stays fast at the intended rate

unit.description: Closed list, from docs/units.md. ADR-0002 D15 chose an enumeration over full UCUM precisely so a typo like `mss` is a parse error rather than a disagreement between consumers.

aggregation.description:
How the indicator is reduced to one number. The set is k6's, which is the one every surveyed tool can serve: p50/p95/p99/p99.9 and any other percentile, avg, min, max, sum, stddev, count, rate.
`rate` reads from the shape it is applied to, as it does in k6: over a `distribution` it is per second, over a `ratio` it is the fraction. k6 resolves the same overload the same way, by the metric's type.

selector.description: Selects time series by attribute. {} means every series. A value of "*" means the attribute is present with any value. Attribute names are not enumerated — they are borrowed from OpenTelemetry, whose values may be strings, numbers or booleans.

annotations.description: The only extension point in the format. The opennfr.io/ prefix is reserved.

displayName.description: Free human-readable text beside the machine identifier, in any script. `name` is restricted so something can point at it; this is for a person to read. It is inert: nothing selected, measured or compared depends on it, and two documents differing only in their display names say the same thing. Keep it to the quantity, not the answer — a name reading '99th percentile under 500 ms' beside threshold: 500 is a second source for one number, and the two diverge the first time the threshold moves.

series.description: A metric and the requests it is measured over.

metric.description: A metric name, borrowed from OpenTelemetry semantic conventions where one exists. This schema does not enumerate metric names and never will: enumerating them would make every new metric a change to the format.
